title: MindPal — Verse for the Day
date_key_rule: YYYY-MM-DD in the user's local calendar (client resolves today)
disclaimer: Supportive wellness reading. Not clinical therapy or religious instruction. Scripture quoted accurately from traditional public texts; reflections are original MindPal. Science-of-mind notes are general established ideas, not specific paper claims. AU urgent help: 000 / Lifeline 13 11 14.

verse.source_note: string — how to treat the quote

verse.text: This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

default.reflection: Begin by noticing that this day is already given. Joy here is a choice of attention, not a demand that everything feel easy.

practice.text: Place a hand on your chest. Breathe out slowly for six counts. Softly say: this day is enough to begin.

verse.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

entries.reflection: Christ’s peace is offered as an inner steadiness, different from circumstances going your way. You can receive calm without pretending hard things are gone.

practice.text: Sit quietly for one minute. On each out-breath, release one tense place in your body. Whisper: peace, here.

verse.text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
verse.source_note: Classical Pali Canon teaching; English rendering of a well-attested verse.

entries.reflection: Meeting irritation with more irritation feeds the loop. Softening does not mean approving harm — it means choosing a response that does not multiply heat.

practice.text: For one minute, notice any irritation as warmth in the body. Name it ‘heat.’ Breathe out and let the shoulders drop.

verse.text: So truly where there is hardship, there is also ease. Truly where there is hardship, there is also ease.
verse.source_note: Qur’anic verse (Surah Ash-Sharh). Use a translation you trust for study; wording here is a careful English rendering of the paired ease-after-hardship lines.

entries.reflection: Hardship and ease are spoken as companions, not as a denial of pain. Today’s difficulty does not cancel the possibility of relief beside it.

practice.text: One minute: breathe in for four, out for six. On the out-breath, silently add: ease is allowed here too.

verse.text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
verse.source_note: Stoic classic; wording follows a widely used modern English sense of the teaching. Not a verse of scripture.

entries.reflection: Strength here is not control of everything — only ownership of your next inner move: attention, judgment, response.

practice.text: For one minute, pick one worry. Label it ‘outside’ or ‘mine to choose.’ If outside, return to one breath.

verse.text: A longer out-breath helps the body shift toward calm: slower exhalation supports parasympathetic settling and can soften stress arousal.
verse.source_note: General, widely taught breath–nervous-system relationship. Not a citation of a specific paper — do not invent study titles.

entries.reflection: You do not need perfect meditation. One honest longer out-breath is a portable practice your nervous system can use today.

practice.text: Breathe in gently for four counts. Breathe out for six to eight. Repeat for one minute without forcing.

verse.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.

entries.reflection: Still waters are an image of guided rest. You can seek a quieter pace without earning it first.

practice.text: One minute of quiet. Imagine still water. Let the jaw unclench on each out-breath.

verse.text: Be kind whenever possible. It is always possible.
verse.reference: Attributed to the Dalai Lama (widely circulated teaching)
verse.source_note: Popular attribution to the 14th Dalai Lama in public talks/writings tradition. Treat as a living wisdom teaching, not scripture.

entries.reflection: Kindness is not weakness. It is a trainable choice that steadies your own mind while softening how you meet others.

practice.text: For one minute, bring one person to mind. Silently wish them one kind thing. Then include yourself.
